contents.name: §5.5 stationary measure and detailed balance definitions
Example 5.5.1, random walk with counting stationary measure
contents.reason: The Z^d random walk with counting stationary measure; the finite doubly-stochastic converse this page does use is proved directly in the doubly-stochastic example, and the general Z^d model is outside the approved inventory.

contents.name: Example 5.5.2, asymmetric simple random walk
contents.reason: The asymmetric nearest-neighbour walk with its non-normalisable geometric stationary measure (p/q)^x; the pair's random-walk counterexample is the symmetric walk on Z, and no planned item states the asymmetric model.

contents.name: Example 5.5.3, the Ehrenfest chain
contents.reason: The Ehrenfest urn model on {0,...,r}; the pair's finite examples are the design's two-state, birth-death, graph-walk and doubly-stochastic items, and no planned item or proof depends on the Ehrenfest chain.

contents.name: Example 5.5.4, birth-and-death detailed-balance weights

Theorem 5.5.6, Kolmogorov cycle criterion for reversibility
contents.reason: The assigned page proves detailed balance and the reversed kernel but does not classify every reversible matrix by products around all directed cycles.

contents.name: Theorem 5.5.7, stationary return-cycle occupation measure
Example 5.5.8, renewal-chain stationary measure
contents.reason: The renewal-chain model is a separate queueing example; the return-cycle construction it illustrates is proved generally in the local lemma.

Example 5.5.13, birth-and-death normalization test
contents.reason: The assigned birth-and-death example has a finite state space. An infinite-state normalization criterion would require its own additional example and is not asserted by the finite formula.

contents.name: Example 5.5.14, M/G/1 queue positive recurrence
contents.reason: The M/G/1 queue and its positive-recurrence threshold mu<1; the pair proves positive recurrence for general irreducible countable chains, and this queueing model with its martingale argument is outside the approved inventory.

contents.name: Theorem 5.5.15, alternative entropy proof of invariant-measure uniqueness
contents.reason: Uniqueness is already proved by the return-cycle minimality argument here; the entropy method is a distinct proof technique with no additional page claim.
